named_after.reverse: Which of these is named after {value}?

rows.label: golden ratio
rows.description: ratio between two quantities whose sum is at the same ratio to the larger one
rows.hook: is a proportion of about 1.618 that shows up in art, architecture and spiral shells

rows.label: Pythagorean theorem
rows.description: relation in Euclidean geometry among the three sides of a right triangle
rows.hook: says the squares on the two shorter sides of a right triangle add up to the square on the longest side

rows.label: tesseract
rows.hook: is the four-dimensional cousin of a cube, often pictured as a cube inside a cube

rows.label: Mandelbrot set
rows.description: fractal-like set that plays a significant role in chaos research
rows.hook: is an endlessly detailed fractal picture that reveals new swirls the more you zoom in

rows.label: Möbius strip
rows.description: two-dimensional surface with only one side and only one edge
rows.hook: is a twisted loop of paper with only one side, made by giving a band a half turn before joining the ends

rows.label: Cartesian coordinate system
rows.description: coordinate system that specifies each point uniquely by a pair of real numbers called coordinates
rows.hook: lays out points on a grid using an x-axis and a y-axis, the graph paper of math class

rows.label: trigonometry
rows.description: branch of mathematics that studies triangles and the relationships between their sides and the angles between these sides
rows.hook: studies the sine, cosine and tangent of angles and how they relate to the sides of triangles

rows.label: Koch snowflake
rows.hook: is a fractal shape with a never-ending, ever-more-jagged six-pointed edge that looks like a frozen crystal

rows.label: torus
rows.description: doughnut-shaped surface of revolution, based on a revolved figure of a circle
rows.hook: is the shape of a doughnut or an inner tube

rows.label: Euclidean geometry
rows.hook: is the classic system of points, lines, angles and circles taught in school, built on a few basic postulates

rows.label: Platonic solid
rows.description: convex regular polyhedra with the same number of faces at each vertex
rows.hook: is one of only five perfectly regular three-dimensional shapes, including the cube and the tetrahedron

rows.label: Voronoi diagram
rows.hook: splits a flat surface into regions, each holding every spot nearest to one of a set of points

rows.label: tessellation
rows.description: tiling of a plane using one or more geometric shapes, called tiles, with no overlaps and no gaps
rows.hook: covers a flat surface with repeating shapes and no gaps, like bathroom floor tiles or an M. C. Escher print

rows.label: Klein bottle
rows.hook: is a one-sided surface with no inside or outside that can't exist in 3D without crossing itself

rows.label: non-Euclidean geometry
rows.description: two geometries based on axioms closely related to those specifying Euclidean geometry
rows.hook: is the kind where parallel lines can meet or diverge, as on a curved surface like a globe
